answers.core:
Modifications to language syntax seem to be a little too significant and far-reaching to be an asset library element. This should be presented as a direct and universal feature.

Additionally, there's nothing saying that a refactored `while`; something I still do myself, sometimes, when I feel that a do loop is being used unnecessarily; can't still be used simply because a `do` loop is available. It would just give the language a little more pliability.
answers.workaround:
As said, the usual workaround is a `while(true)` followed by a conditional break; but after thirty years of programming, that feels like "flying too close to the sun" to me. `while(true)` is generally bad form and bad smell. If I want it to run while variable `c` is not the head of my list, I should have a loop checking against it being equal to the head of the list. Telling the interpreter to always run a loop, and then break out of it in the instructions, is arguably a hack.

If I actually wanted the code to run forever, then `while(true)` might work for me just fine; but here, it doesn't adequately express my will and design as a builder.

title: Implement a do...while loop in GDScript for code readability?
